newsitem.title: USA: Minn. arena funding bill advances in state Senate.
newsitem.headline: Minn. arena funding bill advances in state Senate.

text.p: Minnesota Senate committees have advanced plans for $65 million of state funding for a new downtown St. Paul arena this week, but the proposal must still navigate several obstacles before lawmakers adjourn in a few days, a legislative aide to the sponsor said Friday.

Two senate committees on Thursday advanced a plan to provide a $6.5 million appropriation in fiscal 1998 and a verbal commitment for $58.5 million the following year through a general obligation debt issuance or appropriation from the state general fund, said Kurt Schultz, aide to Sen. Randy Kelly, D-St. Paul.
The plan needs further senate committee approvals on Friday before it can be considered by the full senate and representatives, Schultz said.
St. Paul city officials and lawmakers have been trying to hammer out a public-private financing deal for a $130 million arena to attract a National Hockey League expansion team to Minnesota.
St. Paul has already agreed to provide up to $30 million and the expansion group has pledged $35 million toward an arena to replace the St. Paul Civic Center if the NHL awards a franchise.
St. Paul is one of six finalists for an NHL expansion team. The league has not determined when, or if, it will add teams.
The NHL is also considering bids from groups in Atlanta, Columbus, Ohio, Houston, Nashville and Oklahoma City.

The NHL expansion committee found the existing Civic Center wanting after touring the facility in April. The committee is scheduled to meet again in June and St. Paul officials hope that they will make a recommendation for expansion to the NHL board of governors at that time.
